text: We are developing a screening model that flags adults at high risk of having a stroke, based on their demographics, chronic conditions and lifestyle.
Our cardiology team wants to study how blood sugar, body weight and smoking relate to heart disease in our patient population.
Actuarial project: forecast which members will generate above-median yearly medical charges so that we can plan next year's premiums.
Public-health outreach: estimate which members are likely to be smokers so that we can invite them to a cessation program.
Build a community screening tool that predicts whether a person has diabetes or prediabetes from self-reported health and lifestyle indicators.
Analyse which risk factors, such as blood pressure, cholesterol, smoking and physical activity, predict coronary heart disease or a heart attack.
Develop an early-warning score that predicts in-hospital death for ICU admissions from first-day vital signs, laboratory values and comorbidities.
Estimate which ICU patients will need mechanical ventilation, based on their admission characteristics and first-day physiology.
Quality-improvement study: predict which diabetic inpatients will be readmitted after discharge, using their encounter history, laboratory tests and medications.
Pharmacy review: understand what drives a change of diabetes medication during a hospital stay.
Capacity planning: predict whether a visit will be an emergency, urgent-care or inpatient encounter rather than a routine one, from the patient's background and clinical history.
Cost study: identify patients whose lifetime healthcare expenses are above the median, from their conditions, medications and insurance.
